title: Ratatouille
subtitle: Provençal slow-cooked vegetable stew
excerpt: Aubergine, courgette, pepper, and tomato cooked slowly in olive oil with garlic, thyme, and basil until completely soft and melding together. Better the next day.

recipe.sourceNotes: Ratatouille is a Provençal dish from the Nice area of southern France, first recorded in the 18th century. The name derives from the French 'touiller', meaning to stir or toss. The traditional method requires cooking each vegetable separately in olive oil before combining them, which prevents the individual vegetables from becoming a mush and preserves their distinct characters. A shortcut version cooks them all together, which gives a soft, unified stew rather than a layered result. Both are valid; the separate-cooking method gives a more interesting final dish. Ratatouille improves significantly if eaten the day after it is made.

content.text: Salt the aubergine and leave to drain for 20 minutes before cooking: this draws out bitterness and excess moisture. Cook each vegetable separately in the pan and only combine them at the end: this is the step that makes the difference between a stew and a proper ratatouille. Use good olive oil; it is the dominant flavour of the dish.
Salt the diced aubergine and leave in a colander for 20 minutes. Rinse and pat dry.

Heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a large, wide pan. Fry the aubergine in batches until golden. Remove and set aside. Repeat with the courgette in 2 more tablespoons of oil until golden. Remove and set aside. Fry the peppers in the same way. Remove and set aside.
Heat the remaining oil in the pan. Soften the onion for 8 minutes. Add the garlic, thyme, and bay leaves. Cook for 1 minute. Add the tinned tomatoes. Simmer for 10 minutes.

Return all the vegetables to the pan. Stir gently. Cover and cook over low heat for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until everything is tender. Check seasoning. Remove the thyme and bay leaves. Tear in the basil. Serve warm or at room temperature.
